7. WebGames Benchmark: Limits of Browser AI Agents

SEO Keywords: browser AI benchmarking, AI agent failure modes, web task automation issues

Core Problems & Challenges (Oasis Playbook Lens)

Privacy & Data Control

Both Chrome and Edge collect and use browsing data to power AI features — raising serious transparency and consent challenges that many users don't fully understand or control.

Hallucinations & Misinformation

AI summaries and answers (Gemini in Chrome, Copilot in Edge) risk providing incorrect or misleading content without clear source attribution, undercutting user trust.

Zero-Click Consumption

AI-driven answers reduce traffic to actual websites — threatening publishers and the open Web's economic model.

Security Exploits

Rapid AI integration in Chrome (e.g., malicious extensions exploiting GenAI trends) and Edge raises security vulnerabilities beyond traditional browsing.

Execution Gaps

Even with AI built in, browsers struggle with autonomous task execution and deep multi-step interactions — as seen in AI agent benchmarks — exposing practical limitations.

What Oasis Does Instead (High-Level Playbook)

  • Separation of user intent from untrusted content to reduce prompt-injection risk
  • Transparent privacy controls & explainable AI responses instead of opaque data collection
  • Task automation with fail-safe human approval rather than full unsupervised execution
  • Security-first extension/agent architecture to prevent malicious automation exploit vectors
  • Source-verified reasoning pipelines instead of zero-click summaries that hide web context
